TODO-151 · maps mobile · proof by touch

one finger owns the map.

The gesture config was already greedy — the finish is proving no gate is left. A Pixel 7 Chromium project now drives a real one-finger CDP touch stream against the live app: the camera moves, the page doesn't, and the "two fingers" overlay never shows. The same input against a cooperative build freezes — so the spec discriminates, it doesn't decorate. All on PR #489, CI green.

02the gate, refused

The identical one-finger stream against a build flipped to cooperative — the exact regression this ticket removes. The map shades, demands two fingers, and the camera never leaves 17,0. Run the pan spec against this build and it fails: that's the negative control, and it's how we know the green test means something.

cooperative, mid-drag · blocked
center 17.000000,0.000000 · frozen
Why there's nothing to fight over: in mobile map view the surface is full-height (100dvh − 56px header) and the footer is dropped, so the page has no scroll run-out. Greedy isn't stealing scroll from the page — there is no page left to scroll. That's the TODO-152 surface doing half of TODO-151's job, and the layout specs pin it.

04what it took to fake a finger

Synthetic touch must be paced like a real finger. A raw dispatchTouchEvent loop fires all its moves in a few milliseconds; the Maps gesture recognizer silently drops it — events delivered, camera frozen, nothing in the console. The stream only reads as a drag with a ~120ms press before the first move, moves at ~60Hz, and a beat of settle before release. The helper in mobile-map.e2e.ts encodes that so the next spec doesn't rediscover it the hard way.
Mouse is not a proof. A mouse drag panned the map on the first try all along — only a genuine touch stream exercises the code path cooperative would gate. If the spec had used dragTo, the negative control would never have failed and the test would prove nothing.
